newsitem.title: PERU: Jailed Peruvian rebels confident of release.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Peruvian rebels confident of release.

text.p: Jailed Marxist Peruvian guerrillas shouted defiant slogans at warders on Tuesday, confident their comrades' bold assault of the Japanese ambassador's residence would secure their release, a prison official said.

"They are no longer submissive and shout out slogans of popular struggle," said the National Prisons Institute official, who asked not to be identified. "They are sure they are going to be let out," he said.

He said inmates in one jail were chanting, "The spirit of Che lives on in every guerrilla," referring to legendary Latin American revolutionary Ernesto "Che" Guevara, who was shot after his capture by Bolivian soldiers in 1967.

A well-armed group of about 20 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence on Dec. 17 taking hundreds of VIP hostages in a bid to force the release of more than 400 jailed MRTA comrades.
The guerrillas were still holding around 140 captives on Tuesday but President Alberto Fujimori flatly rejected their demands.

The MRTA prisoners, who include the movement's leader Victor Polay, are held in top-security jails in various parts of the country. The most dangerous rebels are imprisoned at a naval base in the port of Callao which neighbours Lima.
